sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Diagnostic Dilemma: Early-Onset Thrombocytopenia Post-Cardiac Surgery
sections.description: This section establishes the clinical narrative, detailing the patient's preoperative history, the specific cardiac procedure performed, and the unexpected trajectory of his platelet count. It focuses on distinguishing this case from standard post-operative complications by highlighting the 'early-onset' nature of the thrombocytopenia (pre-POD5) and the critical link to preoperative heparin exposure during a diagnostic catheterization.
subtopics: Preoperative context: Atrial fibrillation management and pre-catheterization heparin exposure
Intraoperative details: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and massive unfractionated heparin (UFH) load
Postoperative timeline: The deviation from expected hemodynamic stability to progressive thrombocytopenia
The 'Early-Onset' Red Flag: Why a drop before POD5 suggests prior sensitization rather than new exposure
Initial clinical confusion: Differentiating between surgical stress, sepsis, and drug reactions

sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Spectrum: Classic HIT vs. Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
sections.description: Moving beyond simple definition, this section educates readers on the mechanistic shift from classic heparin-dependent HIT to autoimmune HIT (aHIT). It explains how a subset of antibodies can activate platelets independently of heparin, leading to more severe thrombocytopenia and refractory disease courses, setting the theoretical stage for interpreting the patient's unique lab results.
subtopics: Classic HIT mechanism: PF4/heparin complex formation and FcγRIIa receptor clustering
Autoimmune HIT (aHIT): Pathogenesis of heparin-independent platelet activation
Clinical distinctions: Severity of thrombocytopenia and persistence despite anticoagulation
The concept of 'hyper-reactive' antibodies in aHIT compared to conventional HIT
Why standard timelines fail in aHIT cases

sections.section_title: Advanced Serological Interpretation: Decoding Atypical SRA Profiles
sections.description: This section serves as a technical deep-dive into laboratory diagnostics. It guides learners through reading a complex Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) that does not fit standard criteria. It explains why an 'indeterminate' result actually confirms a diagnosis of severe aHIT when specific patterns like serotonin release at zero heparin concentration are present.
subtopics: Screening tools: Interpreting high-titer PF4/polyanion ELISA results in post-op settings
Confirmatory testing limitations: Understanding false negatives/positives in classic assays
The Gold Standard SRA analysis: Deconstructing the patient's unique profile (release at 0 U/mL UFH)
Fc Receptor Blockade Challenge: Analyzing partial resistance to monoclonal antibody IV.3 inhibition
'Indeterminate' Results as Clues: How atypical SRA kinetics define severe aHIT subtypes

sections.description: Focusing on management complexity, this section outlines the rationale behind switching anticoagulants and adding immunomodulatory therapy. It addresses the challenge of treating a patient with active stroke and severe consumption coagulopathy who fails to respond to initial interventions, emphasizing evidence-based choices between Argatroban and Fondaparinux.
subtopics: Immediate cessation of all heparin products and selection of alternative anticoagulants
